issues.existing: constellation lines and gold star points
issues.observed: There are TWO moons in this sky and keyObjects lists neither. A larger one sits at the upper-left corner and a smaller one lower down at the middle left, just above and left of the figure's head. Both are crescents lit along the LOWER-RIGHT limb with the unlit remainder of the disc faintly visible. The smaller disc is a genuine second moon, not a lens flare: it shows the same crescent limb and the same faint full-disc outline as the larger one.
issues.evidence: Larger moon roughly x=60-230 / y=60-180; smaller moon roughly x=80-260 / y=440-560, in the 560x933 image. Both enlarged 5x and brightened show a bright sickle on the lower-right edge of a dim circular disc — a flare would have no dark limb and no disc edge.
